rounds.title: Textarea baseline
rounds.note: The SDK textarea (et-textarea inside et-form-field), first drawing, drawn by textareaField() from @ethlete/components/design/textarea, which wraps formField() and textarea() from the form-field mock and adds the real form-field-textarea-styles sheet (the form-field mock did not load it), max rows, mixed, et-description and forced states. DOM checked against Storybook Textarea Default, ManualResize, FixedWithMaxRows and Mixed. Box appearance, transparent fill, static label, md size, rows 3 with autosize (field-sizing: content) as the lib default; brand theme, danger as the error theme. Hover is forced on the control frame, focus as data-focused plus focus-visible on the native textarea. Fixtures are fictional: Message, placeholder Write something…, a three-line note to Lena, a ten-line note that grows (long-autosize), the same capped at maxRows 4 (scrolls), autosize off with rows 4 and the vertical resize grip, rows 1, mixed values, no label; required with value Hi and error Write at least 20 characters. Widths 320, 360, 640. Measured in Storybook at 360: line-height 21px at 14px, the same as et-input; maxRows 6 caps at 126px (6 lh) and scrolls inside the frame; the frame block padding is 6px, so the first line starts 7px under the frame top, against 14.5px on et-input (min-height 50px, centered). Colour numbers are the text input r1 ones, same tokens: rest frame 1.26 / 1.73, focus (primary) 1.33 / 13.50, error frame 2.30 / 1.72, placeholder 46 % 3.00 / 4.48, required marker 1.33 / 13.50. Decided rules that arise: Q88 (focus frame in ink, invalid in danger ink) and Q99a (required marker light-dark(ink, primary)). Lib bugs apart: (L1) the same et-description bug as text input r1, no inline start padding, 13px left of label, value and hint; b and c draw it aligned. (L3) a textarea is top-aligned inside the 50px min-height frame with only the 6px block padding: rows 1 in Storybook Default draws above 7px, below 22px, the text sits 7.5px higher than an et-input value beside it; b and c pad the textarea frame to (min-height - 1 lh - 2 border) / 2 = 13.5px, so one row centres and every first line meets the input's. (L4) autosize off, resize vertical: the native textarea has no min-block-size, dragging the grip up in Storybook ManualResize shrinks it to 15px, the placeholder is cut in half while the frame stays 50px; not drawable as a static state. Design: (1) to (4) as text input r1 (rest and error frame under 3:1, placeholder 3.00, readonly looks editable, hover outshines focus in b and c); c carries the same proposals. (5) The resize grip is the Chromium UA glyph at the textarea corner, 13px inside the frame corner, unthemed, it looks lost in the padding. (6) Scrolled content clips at the textarea edge 7px (b: 14.5px) inside the frame border, with no fade; a mid-scroll line is cut sharp. Not checked: the scrollbar look, headless Chromium hides scrollbars, so a capped textarea shows no scrollbar in shots or Storybook probes. Later rounds, left out here: underline, filled, floating and inline labels, sm and lg, data-warning, the counter, RTL.

a.note: Today, the lib as is. Rest frame 1.26 / 1.73, focus and required marker mint 1.33 in light, error frame 2.30 / 1.72, placeholder 3.00 / 4.48, readonly identical to filled; the first line 7px under the frame top (input 14.5px), rows 1 top-aligned 7 / 22 (L3); et-description 13px left of label and hint (L1).

b.note: Pick. a plus Q88 and Q99a, decided rules only, plus the L1 and L3 fixes drawn: focus frame in ink 5.48 in light, invalid in the danger ink; required marker light-dark(ink, primary); et-description aligned; the textarea frame padded to 13.5px block, so rows 1 centres like an input and every first line meets the input's. Rest, error, placeholder and readonly unchanged.

c.note: b plus the text input r1 c proposals, not decided rules: rest frame surface-interaction 4.74 / 6.94, error frame full danger primary 4.83 / 3.71, placeholder 60 % 4.67 / 6.77, dashed readonly frame. In light the rest frame sits close to the focus ink, told apart by hue only.
